text: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on
explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Objectives Resolution on 12 March 1949, laying down the ideological basis of Pakistan's future constitutions.

text: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by
explanation: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan introduced the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly in March 1949.

text: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to
explanation: The Resolution opens by declaring that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Allah Almighty alone, and authority is a sacred trust exercised by the people within His limits.

text: The Objectives Resolution was made a substantive part of the Constitution by
explanation: Until 1985 the Objectives Resolution was only a preamble; the Eighth Amendment inserted it into the operative text of the Constitution.

text: As a substantive part of the 1973 Constitution, the Objectives Resolution appears as
explanation: Article 2A gives the Objectives Resolution the status of a substantive provision of the Constitution.

text: From 1947 until the first Constitution was framed, Pakistan was governed under an adapted version of the
explanation: The Government of India Act 1935, as adapted under the Indian Independence Act 1947, served as Pakistan's interim constitution until 1956.

text: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan was dissolved in 1954 by Governor-General
explanation: Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly in October 1954, a step challenged in the Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan case.

text: The One Unit scheme, merging the provinces of West Pakistan into a single unit, was introduced in
explanation: The One Unit was established in 1955, combining the provinces and states of West Pakistan into one administrative unit.

text: The first Constitution of Pakistan came into force on
explanation: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, the anniversary of the Pakistan Resolution.

text: The Prime Minister of Pakistan when the 1956 Constitution was enforced was
explanation: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali headed the government that framed and enforced the 1956 Constitution.

text: The first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution was
explanation: Iskander Mirza became the first President when the 1956 Constitution replaced the office of Governor-General.

text: The official title 'Islamic Republic of Pakistan' was adopted for the first time in the Constitution of
explanation: The 1956 Constitution formally named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

text: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan was abrogated on
explanation: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution and imposed martial law on 7 October 1958.

text: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan consisted of
explanation: Pakistan's first Constitution contained 234 articles arranged in thirteen parts with six schedules.

text: The Constitution Commission appointed in 1960 to recommend a new constitutional framework was headed by
explanation: Ayub Khan appointed a Constitution Commission in 1960 under Justice Muhammad Shahabuddin, whose report preceded the 1962 Constitution.

text: The form of government provided by the 1962 Constitution was
explanation: The 1962 Constitution concentrated executive authority in a directly responsible President, replacing the parliamentary system of 1956.

text: Under the 1962 Constitution the President was elected by an electoral college composed of
explanation: The elected members of the Basic Democracies system formed the electoral college for the presidency and the legislatures under the 1962 Constitution.

text: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated in 1969 by
explanation: General Yahya Khan abrogated the 1962 Constitution and imposed martial law in March 1969 after Ayub Khan handed over power.

text: The National Assembly passed the 1973 Constitution on
explanation: The Constitution Bill was approved by the National Assembly on 10 April 1973 and enforced later that year.

text: The 1973 Constitution of Pakistan came into force on
explanation: The 1973 Constitution became operative on 14 August 1973, when Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took office as Prime Minister.

text: The first Prime Minister under the 1973 Constitution was
explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto assumed the office of Prime Minister when the 1973 Constitution took effect.

text: The first President under the 1973 Constitution was
explanation: Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry held the largely ceremonial presidency created by the 1973 Constitution.

text: The 1973 Constitution of Pakistan contains
explanation: The 1973 Constitution is arranged in twelve parts containing 280 articles.

text: A bicameral legislature at the centre was provided for the first time by the Constitution of
explanation: The 1973 Constitution created the Senate alongside the National Assembly; the 1956 and 1962 constitutions had single chambers.

text: Under Article 2 of the 1973 Constitution, the state religion of Pakistan is
explanation: Article 2 declares that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.

text: Abrogating or subverting the Constitution amounts to high treason under
explanation: Article 6 declares any act of abrogating, subverting or suspending the Constitution by force to be high treason.

text: Fundamental Rights in the 1973 Constitution are contained in Articles
explanation: Part II Chapter 1 of the Constitution sets out Fundamental Rights in Articles 8 to 28.

text: The right to a fair trial and due process was inserted into the Constitution as
explanation: Article 10A, added by the Eighteenth Amendment in 2010, guarantees the right to a fair trial and due process.

text: Freedom of association and the right to form political parties are guaranteed by
explanation: Article 17 protects freedom of association, including the right of citizens to form or be members of political parties.

text: Freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed by which article of the 1973 Constitution?
explanation: Article 19 guarantees freedom of speech and expression subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.

text: The right to information in matters of public importance is provided by
explanation: Article 19A, inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment, gives every citizen the right to have access to information in all matters of public importance.

text: Equality of all citizens before law is guaranteed by
explanation: Article 25 declares all citizens equal before law and entitled to equal protection of law.

text: Free and compulsory education for children aged five to sixteen years is guaranteed by
explanation: Article 25A, added by the Eighteenth Amendment, obliges the State to provide free and compulsory education to children aged five to sixteen.

text: Which article requires all existing laws to be brought into conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Quran and Sunnah?
explanation: Article 227 requires existing laws to conform to Islamic injunctions and bars enactment of any law repugnant to them.

text: The Council of Islamic Ideology is constituted under which article of the 1973 Constitution?
explanation: Article 228 provides for the constitution of the Council of Islamic Ideology and the appointment of its members.

text: Under Article 251 of the Constitution, the national language of Pakistan is
explanation: Article 251 declares Urdu the national language and required arrangements for its use for official purposes within fifteen years of the commencing day.

text: Defection by a member of Parliament from his political party is dealt with under
explanation: Article 63A allows the party head to declare a defecting member for disqualification, with the matter decided by the Election Commission and appealable to the Supreme Court.

text: A bill to amend the Constitution must be passed by the votes of not less than
options: Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
Three-fourths of the total membership of each House
Two-thirds of a joint sitting only
A simple majority of members present in each House
explanation: Article 239 requires a constitutional amendment bill to be passed by two-thirds of the total membership of each House of Parliament.

text: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be elected President of Pakistan is
explanation: Article 41 requires the President to be a Muslim of not less than forty-five years of age who is qualified to be elected a member of the National Assembly.

text: The term of office of the President of Pakistan is
explanation: Article 44 fixes the President's term at five years from the day he enters upon office.

text: The President of Pakistan is elected by an electoral college consisting of
options: Members of the National Assembly only
Members of both Houses of Parliament only
Members of both Houses of Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies
explanation: Article 41 provides that the President is elected by members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.

text: The President may be removed through impeachment by a resolution passed by
options: A simple majority of a joint sitting
Two-thirds of the total membership of Parliament in a joint sitting
explanation: Article 47 requires not less than two-thirds of the total membership of Parliament, voting in a joint sitting, to remove or impeach the President.

text: Under Article 48 of the Constitution, the President shall generally act
options: On and in accordance with the advice of the Cabinet or the Prime Minister
On the advice of the Chief Justice
On the advice of the Chairman of the Senate
explanation: Article 48 binds the President to act on the advice of the Cabinet or the Prime Minister, except where the Constitution allows him to act in his discretion.

text: An Ordinance promulgated by the President remains in force for
explanation: Under Article 89 an Ordinance stands repealed after 120 days unless extended once for a further 120 days by a resolution of the National Assembly.

text: If the office of President becomes vacant, his functions are performed by the
explanation: Article 49 provides that the Chairman of the Senate, or in his absence the Speaker of the National Assembly, acts as President until a new President is elected.

text: The total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan after the Twenty-fifth Amendment is
explanation: The merger of FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa reduced the National Assembly from 342 to 336 seats.

text: The number of seats reserved for women in the National Assembly is
explanation: Article 51 reserves sixty seats in the National Assembly for women, filled through proportional representation from party lists.

text: The number of seats reserved for non-Muslims in the National Assembly is
explanation: Ten National Assembly seats are reserved for non-Muslims under Article 51.

text: The total membership of the Senate of Pakistan after the Twenty-fifth Amendment is
explanation: The Twenty-fifth Amendment abolished the four Senate seats of FATA and reduced the House from 104 to 96 members.

text: The term of office of a member of the Senate of Pakistan is
explanation: Senators are elected for six years, with half the House retiring every three years.

text: Each province is represented in the Senate of Pakistan by
explanation: Each Provincial Assembly elects 23 senators, comprising 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrats or ulema and 1 non-Muslim member.

text: The normal term of the National Assembly of Pakistan is
explanation: Article 52 fixes the National Assembly's term at five years from the day of its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.

text: The minimum age for election as a member of the National Assembly is
explanation: Article 62 requires a candidate for the National Assembly to be not less than twenty-five years of age.

text: The minimum voting age for elections to the National Assembly of Pakistan is
explanation: Citizens of Pakistan who are not less than eighteen years of age and enrolled on the electoral roll may vote.

text: Under the 1973 Constitution a money bill may originate only in the
explanation: Article 73 provides that a money bill originates in the National Assembly; the Senate may only make recommendations on it.

text: Under the 1973 Constitution, the office of Prime Minister of Pakistan can be held only by
options: A person of at least forty-five years of age
explanation: Article 91 requires that the Prime Minister be a Muslim, as does Article 41 for the President.

text: A vote of no-confidence against the Prime Minister is provided for in
explanation: Article 95 lays down the procedure for a resolution of no-confidence against the Prime Minister in the National Assembly.

text: The Prime Minister of Pakistan is elected by
options: A majority of the total membership of the National Assembly
A majority of the members present in the National Assembly
explanation: Article 91 requires the Prime Minister to secure the votes of a majority of the total membership of the National Assembly.

text: Under the Eighteenth Amendment, the total strength of the federal Cabinet including Ministers of State may not exceed
options: 15 per cent of the total membership of Parliament
20 per cent of the National Assembly
11 per cent of the total membership of Parliament
explanation: Article 92 caps the federal Cabinet, including Ministers of State, at eleven per cent of the total membership of Parliament.

text: A Proclamation of Emergency on account of war, external aggression or internal disturbance is issued under
explanation: Article 232 empowers the President to proclaim an emergency when the security of Pakistan is threatened by war, external aggression or internal disturbance beyond a province's control.

text: Command and control of the Armed Forces of Pakistan is dealt with in which article of the Constitution?
explanation: Article 243 vests control and command of the Armed Forces in the Federal Government and provides for the appointment of the services chiefs.

text: The writ jurisdiction of a High Court is derived from which article of the Constitution?
explanation: Article 199 empowers a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of rights within its territorial jurisdiction.

text: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in questions of public importance concerning fundamental rights arises under
explanation: Article 184(3) allows the Supreme Court to act where a question of public importance relating to the enforcement of fundamental rights is involved.

text: The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, exercised on a reference by the President, is contained in
explanation: Article 186 allows the President to refer a question of law of public importance to the Supreme Court for its opinion.

text: A judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan retires at the age of
explanation: Article 179 fixes the retirement age of a Supreme Court judge at sixty-five years.

text: The Supreme Judicial Council of Pakistan is provided for in
explanation: Article 209 establishes the Supreme Judicial Council to inquire into the capacity or conduct of judges of the superior courts.

text: The Supreme Judicial Council consists of the Chief Justice of Pakistan,
options: The Chief Justices of all High Courts
Two next most senior Supreme Court judges and two most senior High Court Chief Justices
The Attorney General and the Federal Law Minister
Four judges nominated by the President
explanation: Article 209 composes the Council of the Chief Justice of Pakistan, the two next most senior judges of the Supreme Court and the two most senior Chief Justices of the High Courts.

text: The Federal Shariat Court of Pakistan was established in
explanation: The Federal Shariat Court was created in 1980 to examine whether laws are repugnant to the injunctions of Islam.

text: The Judicial Commission of Pakistan for the appointment of superior court judges was created by inserting
explanation: Article 175A, inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment, established the Judicial Commission and the Parliamentary Committee for judicial appointments.

text: The permanent seat of the Supreme Court of Pakistan is at
explanation: The Constitution places the seat of the Supreme Court at Islamabad, with registries in the provincial capitals.

text: The Council of Common Interests is constituted under which article of the 1973 Constitution?
explanation: Article 153 provides for the constitution of the Council of Common Interests by the President.

text: The Council of Common Interests is chaired by the
explanation: Since the Eighteenth Amendment the Prime Minister is the chairman of the Council of Common Interests.

text: The Council of Common Interests consists of how many members in total?
explanation: The Council has eight members: the Prime Minister as chairman, the four Chief Ministers and three members of the Federal Government nominated by the Prime Minister.

text: The Constitution requires the Council of Common Interests to meet at least once in every
explanation: Article 154 obliges the Council of Common Interests to meet at least once in ninety days.

text: Under the Constitution the Council of Common Interests is responsible to
explanation: Article 154 makes the Council of Common Interests responsible to Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament), to which it submits an annual report.

text: A complaint by a province about interference with its water supplies is referred under Article 155 to the
explanation: Article 155 provides that such a complaint is made to the Council of Common Interests, which may appoint a commission to investigate it.

text: The National Economic Council under Article 156 of the Constitution is headed by the
explanation: Since the Eighteenth Amendment the Prime Minister chairs the National Economic Council, which reviews the overall economic condition of the country.

text: Under Article 160 the National Finance Commission must be constituted at intervals not exceeding
explanation: Article 160 requires the President to constitute a National Finance Commission at intervals not exceeding five years.

text: The National Finance Commission is chaired by the
options: Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan
explanation: The Federal Minister for Finance heads the National Finance Commission, whose other members include the provincial finance ministers.

text: Under the Seventh National Finance Commission Award the provincial share in the divisible pool was raised to
explanation: The Seventh NFC Award increased the provinces' share of the divisible pool to 57.5 per cent from the second year of the award.

text: In the Seventh NFC Award the weight assigned to population in the horizontal distribution among provinces was
explanation: The Seventh NFC Award used multiple criteria for the first time, giving population 82 per cent weight alongside poverty, revenue generation and inverse population density.

text: The Eighteenth Amendment added a clause to Article 160 providing that a province's share in each NFC award shall not be
options: Less than its share in the previous award
explanation: Article 160(3A) guarantees that the share of the provinces in each successive award shall not be less than that given in the previous award.

text: Under Article 161 the net proceeds of the excise duty on natural gas and the royalty on crude oil are paid to
options: The province in which the well-head is situated
explanation: Article 161 assigns these proceeds to the province in which the well-head of natural gas or crude oil is located.

text: Under Article 172(3), inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment, mineral oil and natural gas within a province vest
options: Jointly and equally in the province and the Federal Government
In the Council of Common Interests
explanation: Article 172(3) gives the province concerned and the Federal Government joint and equal ownership of mineral oil and natural gas within the province.

text: The Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan is appointed by the
explanation: Article 213 provides that the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President following the consultation procedure laid down in the Constitution.

text: The Election Commission of Pakistan consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and
explanation: Article 218 composes the Commission of the Chief Election Commissioner as chairman and four members, one from each province.

text: The term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan is
explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment fixed the Chief Election Commissioner's term at five years.

text: A general election must be held within how many days of the expiry of the National Assembly's term?
explanation: Article 224 requires a general election within sixty days of the natural expiry of the Assembly's term.

text: Detailed constitutional provisions for the appointment of caretaker governments were introduced by the
explanation: The Twentieth Amendment of 2012 laid down the procedure for appointing caretaker Prime Ministers and Chief Ministers in consultation with the opposition.

text: Under Article 226 of the Constitution all elections are held by secret ballot except the election of the
explanation: Article 226 exempts the elections of the Prime Minister and the Chief Ministers from the requirement of a secret ballot.

text: Which article of the Constitution obliges each province to establish a local government system and devolve authority to elected local representatives?
explanation: Article 140A requires every province to establish a local government system and devolve political, administrative and financial responsibility to elected representatives.

text: Under the Eighteenth Amendment, elections to local governments in Pakistan are to be held by the
explanation: Clause (2) of Article 140A, added in 2010, assigns the conduct of local government elections to the Election Commission of Pakistan.

text: The Governor of a province is appointed by the
explanation: Article 101 provides that the President appoints the Governor of a province on the advice of the Prime Minister.

text: A Chief Minister of a province is elected by
options: A majority of members present in the Provincial Assembly
The Prime Minister on the Governor's advice
A majority of the total membership of the Provincial Assembly
explanation: Article 130 requires the Chief Minister to be elected by the votes of a majority of the total membership of the Provincial Assembly.

text: Where a provincial law is inconsistent with an Act of Parliament that Parliament is competent to enact, the Constitution provides that
options: The matter goes to the Council of Common Interests
explanation: Article 143 provides that the Act of Parliament prevails and the inconsistent provincial law is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

text: The Auditor-General of Pakistan is appointed by the
explanation: Article 168 provides for the appointment of the Auditor-General of Pakistan by the President.

text: The power of the President to dissolve the National Assembly in his discretion under Article 58(2)(b) was introduced by the
explanation: The Eighth Amendment of 1985 inserted Article 58(2)(b), giving the President discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly.

text: Article 58(2)(b) was deleted from the Constitution in 1997 by the
explanation: The Thirteenth Amendment, passed in 1997, stripped the President of the discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly.

text: The Fourteenth Amendment of 1997 was primarily concerned with
options: Disqualification of members on defection from their party
explanation: The Fourteenth Amendment introduced anti-defection provisions to prevent floor crossing by legislators.

text: The Seventeenth Amendment, passed in 2003, is best known for
options: Restoring the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly
Creating the Council of Common Interests
explanation: The Seventeenth Amendment revived Article 58(2)(b) and validated the Legal Framework Order issued during General Musharraf's rule.

text: The Eighteenth Amendment to the Constitution of Pakistan was passed in
explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment was approved by Parliament and assented to in April 2010.

text: The Concurrent Legislative List was abolished by the
explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment deleted the Concurrent Legislative List, transferring its subjects to the provinces.

text: The North-West Frontier Province was renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by the
explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment of 2010 changed the name of the North-West Frontier Province to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

text: The parliamentary committee that drafted the Eighteenth Amendment was chaired by
explanation: Senator Mian Raza Rabbani headed the Parliamentary Committee on Constitutional Reforms that produced the Eighteenth Amendment.

text: The Twenty-first Amendment to the Constitution was passed to
options: Establish military courts for terrorism cases
Create the office of caretaker Prime Minister
Fix the tenure of the Chief Justice
explanation: Passed in January 2015 after the Peshawar school attack, the Twenty-first Amendment allowed military courts to try terrorism suspects.

text: The Twenty-first Amendment contained a sunset clause under which it was to expire after
explanation: The military courts created by the Twenty-first Amendment were given a life of two years from the date of commencement.

text: The Twenty-fifth Amendment to the Constitution of Pakistan provided for the
options: Creation of the Council of Common Interests
Merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
explanation: The Twenty-fifth Amendment of 2018 merged the Federally Administered Tribal Areas into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and omitted Article 247.

text: The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution, passed in 1974, dealt with
explanation: The Second Amendment amended Article 260 to define who is a Muslim, declaring Ahmadis to be non-Muslims for constitutional purposes.

text: The Twenty-sixth Amendment of 2024 fixed the tenure of the Chief Justice of Pakistan at
explanation: The Twenty-sixth Amendment limited the Chief Justice of Pakistan to a three-year term and provided for constitutional benches in the Supreme Court.

text: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
explanation: Sir Syed died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh and was buried beside the mosque of the college he had founded.

text: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was established in which year?
explanation: Sir Syed opened the school at Aligarh in 1875, which was raised to the status of a college in 1877.

text: Which book did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan write to explain the causes of the 1857 uprising?
explanation: In Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind Sir Syed argued that British ignorance of Indian feeling, not Muslim disloyalty, had caused the revolt.

text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan launched the magazine Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq in which year?
explanation: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was started in 1870 to promote social and intellectual reform among Indian Muslims.

text: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society in 1864 at which place?
explanation: The Scientific Society was established at Ghazipur in 1864 to translate Western works on science into Urdu, and was later moved to Aligarh.

text: The Urdu-Hindi controversy of 1867, which deepened Sir Syed's belief in Muslim separateness, began in which city?
explanation: A movement at Banaras in 1867 demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in the courts, convincing Sir Syed that Hindus and Muslims could not remain one nation.

text: The Muhammadan Educational Conference was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in which year?
explanation: Founded in 1886, the Muhammadan Educational Conference met annually across India to spread modern education among Muslims and later provided the platform on which the Muslim League was formed.

text: Which Viceroy ordered the partition of Bengal in 1905?
explanation: Lord Curzon carried out the partition of Bengal on administrative grounds, dividing a province that was too large to govern effectively.

text: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October of which year?
explanation: The partition became effective on 16 October 1905, a day observed by Hindu opponents as a day of mourning.

text: What was the capital of the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam created in 1905?
explanation: Dacca became the capital of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving the Muslim-majority east its own administrative centre.

text: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
explanation: The partition was reversed in 1911 in the face of sustained Hindu agitation, which convinced Muslims that British assurances were unreliable.

text: Which Muslim leader of Dacca was the strongest supporter of the partition of Bengal?
explanation: Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dacca championed the partition because it gave the Muslims of eastern Bengal an administration of their own.

text: The Simla Deputation waited upon the Viceroy on 1 October of which year?
explanation: The deputation of Muslim notables met the Viceroy at Simla on 1 October 1906, three months before the Muslim League was founded.

text: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906?
explanation: Sir Aga Khan III headed the deputation and read the address presented to the Viceroy.

text: How many members made up the Simla Deputation of 1906?
explanation: Thirty-five Muslim leaders drawn from all provinces of India formed the deputation that met Lord Minto.

text: The central demand of the Simla Deputation was for
options: Urdu as the official language of India
the abolition of the zamindari system
explanation: The deputation asked that Muslims be given separate electorates and weightage in representation because of their political importance, a demand conceded in 1909.

text: The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December of which year?
explanation: The League was founded on 30 December 1906 during the annual session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference.

text: In which city was the All India Muslim League founded?
explanation: The League was founded at Dacca, where the Muhammadan Educational Conference was holding its annual session.

text: Who was the first President of the All India Muslim League?
explanation: Sir Aga Khan III was chosen as the first President of the League and held the office until 1912.

text: The London branch of the All India Muslim League was established in 1908 by
explanation: Syed Ameer Ali set up the League's London branch in 1908 to present the Muslim case before British opinion.

text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah formally joined the All India Muslim League in which year?
explanation: Jinnah joined the League in 1913 after it adopted self-government as its aim, while retaining his Congress membership for some years.

text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December of which year?
explanation: Jinnah was born at Karachi on 25 December 1876.

text: Jinnah was first elected to the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910 as a Muslim member from
explanation: Jinnah entered the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910 as the Muslim member for Bombay.

text: Which measure did Jinnah pilot through the Imperial Legislative Council in 1913 to protect Muslim family endowments?
explanation: Jinnah secured passage of the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, commonly called the Wakf Alal Aulad Act, restoring the legality of family endowments.

text: The Lucknow Pact was concluded in which year?
explanation: The Congress and the Muslim League concluded the Lucknow Pact in December 1916 on a joint scheme of constitutional reform.

text: Under the Lucknow Pact the Indian National Congress for the first time accepted
explanation: The chief Muslim gain from the Lucknow Pact was Congress recognition of separate electorates and of weightage for Muslims in minority provinces.

text: Who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh?
explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer commanded the troops that fired on the crowd at Jallianwala Bagh.

text: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced which system in the provinces?
explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy, dividing provincial subjects into reserved and transferred halves.

text: The Khilafat Movement was launched in which year?
explanation: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 to defend the Ottoman Caliphate after the Turkish defeat in the First World War.

text: The All India Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919 in which city?
explanation: The All India Khilafat Committee was set up at Bombay in 1919 to organise the movement and raise funds for it.

text: The 'Ali Brothers' of the Khilafat Movement were
options: Zafar Ali Khan and Shaukat Ali
Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Zafar Ali Khan
Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali
Shaukat Ali and Syed Ameer Ali
explanation: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali led the Khilafat agitation and were known as the Ali Brothers.

text: The Hijrat Movement of 1920 involved the migration of Indian Muslims to
explanation: Thousands of Muslims left for Afghanistan in 1920 after India was declared dar-ul-harb, but the migration ended in hardship and failure.

text: The newspaper 'Al-Hilal' was launched in 1912 by
explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad brought out Al-Hilal from Calcutta in 1912, giving Urdu journalism a militant anti-British tone.

text: The Simon Commission was appointed by the British government in which year?
explanation: The commission was appointed in 1927 to review the working of the 1919 reforms and reached India in 1928.

text: Indian parties boycotted the Simon Commission chiefly because
options: it recommended the partition of India
it proposed to abolish separate electorates
it was headed by a serving general
explanation: All seven members of the commission were British, which Indians of every party resented as a denial of their fitness to shape their own constitution.

text: The committee that produced the Nehru Report of 1928 was chaired by
explanation: Motilal Nehru chaired the committee appointed by the All Parties Conference to draft a constitution for India.

text: On the question of representation, the Nehru Report recommended
options: reservation of half the seats for Muslims
explanation: The report proposed joint electorates with reservation in some cases, which Muslims saw as the withdrawal of the safeguard granted in 1909 and confirmed in 1916.

text: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in which year?
explanation: Jinnah placed the Fourteen Points before the Muslim League in March 1929 as the Muslim answer to the Nehru Report.

text: One of Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded that Muslim representation in the central legislature should not be less than
explanation: The points required that Muslims be given not less than one-third of the seats in the central legislature.

text: The Delhi Muslim Proposals were put forward by Jinnah in which year?
explanation: In 1927 Jinnah offered to give up separate electorates in return for stated safeguards, an offer set aside after the Nehru Report.

text: Allama Iqbal delivered his famous Allahabad Address in which year?
explanation: Iqbal delivered the address in December 1930, outlining the idea of a consolidated Muslim state in north-western India.

text: In the Allahabad Address Iqbal proposed the amalgamation of which areas into a single state?
options: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan
explanation: Iqbal called for the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan to be amalgamated into a single state.

text: Allama Iqbal died on
explanation: Iqbal died at Lahore on 21 April 1938, nine years before the state he had envisaged came into being.

text: Allama Iqbal obtained his doctorate from a university in which city?
explanation: Iqbal took his doctorate from the University of Munich in 1908 with a thesis on the development of metaphysics in Persia.

text: Allama Iqbal was knighted in which year?
explanation: Iqbal received a knighthood in 1922 in recognition of his poetry and scholarship.

text: Which party boycotted the First Round Table Conference of 1930-31?
explanation: The Congress stayed away from the First Round Table Conference because its leaders were in jail during the civil disobedience movement.

text: Gandhi personally attended which Round Table Conference?
explanation: Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference of 1931 as the sole representative of the Congress.

text: Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference followed which agreement?
explanation: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 civil disobedience was suspended and the Congress agreed to attend the conference.

text: The Third Round Table Conference was held in which year?
explanation: The third and last conference met in London late in 1932 and was attended by only a small number of delegates.

text: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by the British Prime Minister
explanation: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932 after the Round Table Conferences failed to reach a communal settlement.

text: The name 'Pakistan' was coined by
explanation: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name in 1933 in a pamphlet issued from Cambridge.

text: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet of 1933 in which the name Pakistan first appeared was titled
explanation: The pamphlet Now or Never, issued on 28 January 1933, first used the word Pakistan for the Muslim homeland in north-western India.

text: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced which system in the provinces?
options: Nomination of ministers by the Viceroy
explanation: The Act of 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and gave the provinces autonomy under ministers responsible to elected legislatures.

text: Under the constitutional changes of the mid-1930s, Sindh was made a separate province by separating it from
explanation: Sindh, long a part of the Bombay Presidency, became a separate province in 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.

text: The Muslim League observed the 'Day of Deliverance' on 22 December of which year?
explanation: Jinnah called for a Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 after the Congress ministries resigned.

text: The Pirpur Report of 1938 dealt with
options: Muslim grievances under the Congress ministries
the demarcation of the Punjab boundary
explanation: The committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur inquired into Muslim complaints against the Congress provincial governments.

text: The Sikandar-Jinnah Pact was concluded in which year?
explanation: Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan agreed in 1937 that Muslim members of his Unionist Party would join the Muslim League, greatly strengthening it in the Punjab.

text: A. K. Fazlul Haq was popularly known as
explanation: Fazlul Haq, Premier of Bengal, was called Sher-e-Bengal, the Lion of Bengal.

text: Jinnah returned permanently from England to India to reorganise the Muslim League in
explanation: Jinnah gave up his London practice and returned in 1934, when he was elected permanent president of the Muslim League.

text: Liaquat Ali Khan became Honorary General Secretary of the All India Muslim League in
explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was elected general secretary in 1936 and held the office until independence.

text: The Lahore Resolution was passed on
explanation: The resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940 on the concluding day of the League's Lahore session.

text: The Lahore Resolution of 1940 was moved by
explanation: A. K. Fazlul Haq, then Premier of Bengal, moved the resolution before the Lahore session.

text: The Lahore session of the Muslim League in March 1940 was presided over by
explanation: Jinnah presided over the Lahore session and in his address set out the case that Muslims were a nation by every definition.

text: The Lahore Resolution was passed at which ground in Lahore?
explanation: The session was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where the Minar-e-Pakistan later marked the spot.

text: The Delhi Convention of Muslim League legislators in April 1946 amended the Lahore Resolution to demand
options: dominion status within the British Empire
a federation with India at the centre
a single independent state of Pakistan
explanation: The 1946 convention replaced the wording about independent states with the demand for one sovereign state of Pakistan comprising the Muslim-majority zones.

text: Which was the first provincial legislature in British India to pass a resolution in favour of Pakistan?
explanation: The Sindh Legislative Assembly was the first to adopt a resolution supporting the demand for Pakistan.

text: The Cripps Mission came to India in which year?
explanation: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in March 1942 with proposals meant to secure Indian support for the war effort.

text: Who described the Cripps proposals as 'a post-dated cheque'?
explanation: Gandhi dismissed the offer of dominion status after the war as a post-dated cheque, because nothing was to be conceded immediately.

text: The Quit India Movement was launched in August of which year?
explanation: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in August 1942, after which its leadership was imprisoned for the rest of the war.

text: The C. R. Formula of 1944 was an attempt to settle the deadlock between
options: the British government and the Congress
the Congress and the princely states
the Muslim League and the Sikhs
the Congress and the Muslim League
explanation: C. Rajagopalachari's formula offered a plebiscite in the Muslim-majority districts in return for League cooperation, and formed the basis of the Gandhi-Jinnah talks.

text: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 were held in which city?
explanation: Gandhi met Jinnah at Jinnah's Bombay residence in September 1944, but the talks broke down over the definition of Pakistan.

text: The Simla Conference of 1945 was convened by which Viceroy?
explanation: Lord Wavell called the Simla Conference in June 1945 to form a new Executive Council of Indian members.

text: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed mainly because of a disagreement over
options: the Muslim League's claim to nominate all Muslim members of the Executive Council
the date of British withdrawal from India
the future of the princely states
explanation: Jinnah insisted that the League alone could nominate the Muslim members, a claim the Congress refused to accept, and the conference collapsed.

text: In the elections to the Central Legislative Assembly held in 1945-46, the Muslim League won
options: twenty of the thirty Muslim seats
twenty-five of the thirty Muslim seats
explanation: The League captured every one of the thirty Muslim seats in the central assembly, establishing its claim to speak for Indian Muslims.

text: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Lahore Resolution was passed?
explanation: Lord Linlithgow was Viceroy from 1936 to 1943 and therefore held office in March 1940.

text: The Cabinet Mission reached India in which month and year?
explanation: The three British ministers arrived in India in March 1946 to negotiate the transfer of power.

text: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was headed by
explanation: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, the Secretary of State for India, led the mission as its senior member.

text: The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on
explanation: The mission published its own plan on 16 May 1946 after the Simla talks between the Congress and the League failed.

text: Into how many groups or sections did the Cabinet Mission Plan divide the provinces of British India?
explanation: The plan placed the provinces in three sections, labelled A, B and C, within a loose federation.

text: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, Group B was to consist of
options: Bombay, Madras and the United Provinces
the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province and Sindh
explanation: Group B comprised the Muslim-majority provinces of the north-west, while Group C contained Bengal and Assam.

text: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on
explanation: Direct Action Day was observed on 16 August 1946 and was followed by severe rioting in Calcutta.

text: The Muslim League called Direct Action Day after withdrawing its acceptance of
explanation: The League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan when the Congress placed its own interpretation on the grouping clauses.

text: The Interim Government took office on 2 September of which year?
explanation: The Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru was sworn in on 2 September 1946, and the Muslim League joined it in October.

text: Which portfolio did Liaquat Ali Khan hold in the Interim Government of 1946?
explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan took charge of Finance and used the department to demonstrate the League's weight within the Interim Government.

text: Prime Minister Attlee announced Britain's intention to transfer power in India by June 1948 on
explanation: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 fixed a deadline for withdrawal and announced the appointment of a new Viceroy.

text: Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
explanation: Lord Mountbatten succeeded Lord Wavell in March 1947 and presided over the transfer of power.

text: The plan for the partition of India announced on 3 June 1947 is also known as the
explanation: The 3 June Plan, drawn up under Lord Mountbatten, provided the scheme by which British India was divided.

text: Under the 3 June Plan a referendum was to be held in the North-West Frontier Province and in
explanation: Referendums were prescribed for the North-West Frontier Province and for the Sylhet district of Assam.

text: The referendum in the North-West Frontier Province was held in which month of 1947?
explanation: The referendum took place in July 1947 and returned a large majority in favour of joining Pakistan, though the Khudai Khidmatgars boycotted it.

text: The 1947 referendum in Sylhet resulted in the district joining
explanation: Sylhet voted to leave Assam and join East Bengal, and so became part of Pakistan.

text: The decision of British Balochistan to join Pakistan in 1947 was taken by
explanation: The Shahi Jirga of Quetta, together with the non-official members of the Quetta municipality, voted in June 1947 for accession to Pakistan.

text: The Indian Independence Act received the royal assent on
explanation: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act, which received the royal assent on 18 July 1947.

text: Who was appointed chairman of the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions?
explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired both boundary commissions, and the resulting line bears his name.

text: The Radcliffe Award was made public on
explanation: The boundary award was published on 17 August 1947, three days after Pakistan came into being.

text: Apart from its chairman, each Boundary Commission of 1947 consisted of how many members?
explanation: Each commission had four members, two nominated by the Congress and two by the Muslim League, so the chairman's casting voice decided every disputed point.

text: Which Muslim-majority district was controversially awarded to India by the Radcliffe Award?
explanation: Most of Gurdaspur district went to India despite its Muslim majority, giving India a land route to Kashmir.

text: Pakistan came into being on
explanation: Pakistan's independence was celebrated on 14 August 1947, the day the transfer of power took effect for the new dominion.

text: Jinnah took the oath as the first Governor-General of Pakistan on
explanation: Jinnah was sworn in as Governor-General on 15 August 1947, the day after the independence celebrations.

text: Who was elected the first President of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
explanation: Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947 and delivered his celebrated address on that occasion.

text: In his address to the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947 Jinnah stressed
options: freedom of religion for every citizen of the new state
the abolition of the princely states
the recovery of Kashmir by force
explanation: Jinnah told the Assembly that every citizen was free to go to his temple or mosque and that religion had nothing to do with the business of the state.

text: The Darul Uloom at Deoband was founded in 1866 by
explanation: Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautvi established the seminary at Deoband in 1866 to preserve traditional Islamic learning after 1857.

text: The Nadwatul Ulema was established in 1894 at
explanation: The Nadwatul Ulema was founded at Lucknow with the aim of combining religious learning with modern subjects.

text: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam was founded in 1884 in which city?
explanation: The Anjuman-i-Himayat-i-Islam was set up at Lahore to promote education among Muslims and to counter missionary activity.

text: The Faraizi Movement in Bengal was founded by
explanation: Haji Shariatullah began the Faraizi Movement in Bengal to make Muslims observe the obligatory duties of Islam and to resist landlord oppression.

text: Syed Ahmad Barelvi was killed in 1831 in the battle of
explanation: Syed Ahmad Barelvi and Shah Ismail Shaheed fell at Balakot in 1831 fighting the Sikh forces.

text: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with the help of
explanation: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, took the leading part in organising the Congress in 1885.

text: The Khudai Khidmatgar movement was founded by
explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan organised the Khudai Khidmatgars, known as the Red Shirts, in the North-West Frontier Province and allied them with the Congress.

text: Who was the first Muslim to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress?
explanation: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the Congress session of 1887 at Madras, the first Muslim to hold that office.

text: The Khaksar Movement was founded by
explanation: Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi founded the Khaksar Movement, whose members drilled with spades as a symbol of service and discipline.

text: The highest mountain peak of Pakistan is
explanation: K2, at 8,611 metres, is the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world after Mount Everest.

text: K2 is situated in which mountain range?
explanation: K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China frontier in Gilgit-Baltistan.

text: Nanga Parbat lies in which mountain range?
explanation: Nanga Parbat, 8,126 metres high, is the western anchor of the Himalayan range and lies in Diamer district.

text: The highest peak of the Hindu Kush range is
explanation: Tirich Mir, 7,708 metres, in Chitral district is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

text: How many peaks above 8,000 metres are located in Pakistan?
explanation: Pakistan has five eight-thousanders: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II.

text: The Siachen Glacier lies in which mountain range?
explanation: Siachen is a long glacier of the eastern Karakoram range and is the world's highest battleground.

text: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with
explanation: The Khunjerab Pass in Gilgit-Baltistan is the border crossing between Pakistan and China's Xinjiang region.

text: The Khyber Pass links Pakistan with
explanation: The Khyber Pass runs from Peshawar valley through the Safed Koh to Afghanistan and has been the historic invasion route into the subcontinent.

text: The Shandur Pass connects Chitral with
explanation: Shandur, the site of the world's highest polo ground, links Chitral with Gilgit.

text: The Lowari Pass provides a route between Chitral and
explanation: The Lowari Pass, now bypassed by the Lowari Tunnel, connects Chitral with the Dir district.

text: The Babusar Pass links the Kaghan Valley with
explanation: Babusar Top joins the upper Kaghan Valley to Chilas on the Karakoram Highway.

text: The Indus River rises in
explanation: The Indus originates in the Tibetan plateau near Lake Mansarovar before entering Gilgit-Baltistan.

text: The Kabul River joins the Indus at
explanation: The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock, just below Khairabad.

text: The Panjnad River joins the Indus near
explanation: The combined waters of the five eastern rivers form the Panjnad, which enters the Indus at Mithankot.

text: Tarbela Dam is built on which river?
explanation: Tarbela, in Swabi district, is an earth-filled dam on the Indus completed in 1976.

text: Mangla Dam is constructed on which river?
explanation: Mangla Dam, completed in 1967, impounds the Jhelum River near Mirpur in Azad Kashmir.

text: Warsak Dam has been built on which river?
explanation: Warsak Dam lies on the Kabul River about twenty kilometres from Peshawar.

text: The Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being constructed on which river?
explanation: Diamer-Bhasha is a concrete gravity dam on the Indus upstream of Tarbela.

text: The Mohmand Dam is being built on which river?
explanation: Mohmand Dam is a hydropower and storage project on the Swat River in Mohmand district.

text: The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus was completed in
explanation: Formerly called the Lloyd Barrage, Sukkur Barrage was completed in 1932 and feeds one of the world's largest irrigation systems.

text: The Ghulam Muhammad Barrage on the Indus is commonly known as
explanation: Kotri Barrage near Hyderabad is officially named the Ghulam Muhammad Barrage and is the lowest barrage on the Indus.

text: The largest desert of Pakistan is the
explanation: The Thar Desert of southeastern Sindh is the largest desert in Pakistan and extends into Indian Rajasthan.

text: The Thal Desert lies between the Indus and which other river?
explanation: Thal occupies the doab between the Indus and the Jhelum in districts such as Bhakkar and Layyah.

text: The largest freshwater lake of Pakistan is
explanation: Manchar Lake in Sindh, west of the Indus, is the largest natural freshwater lake in Pakistan.

text: Keenjhar Lake mainly supplies drinking water to which city?
explanation: Keenjhar (Kalri) Lake in Thatta district is the principal source of piped water for Karachi.

text: Lake Saiful Muluk is located in which valley?
explanation: Saiful Muluk is an alpine lake near Naran in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

text: Attabad Lake, formed by a landslide in 2010, lies in which valley?
explanation: A massive landslide at Attabad in January 2010 blocked the Hunza River and created the lake.

text: Hanna Lake is situated near which city?
explanation: Hanna Lake lies in the Urak valley a short distance from Quetta.

text: The largest province of Pakistan by area is
explanation: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square kilometres, roughly 44 per cent of Pakistan's territory.

text: The total area of Pakistan is approximately
explanation: Pakistan's area is officially given as 796,096 square kilometres.

text: The length of Pakistan's coastline is approximately
explanation: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline of about 1,046 kilometres is shared between Sindh and Balochistan.

text: Pakistan's shortest international land border is with
explanation: The Pakistan-China boundary along the Karakoram is the shortest of Pakistan's land borders.

text: The Durand Line between Pakistan and Afghanistan was demarcated in
explanation: The line was agreed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.

text: The Sir Creek dispute concerns the boundary between Sindh and the Indian state of
explanation: Sir Creek is a tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch marking the disputed Sindh-Gujarat maritime boundary.

text: Gwadar was purchased by Pakistan in 1958 from
explanation: Gwadar had been an enclave of the Sultanate of Oman and was bought by Pakistan in 1958.

text: Port Qasim is located near which city?
explanation: Port Qasim, Pakistan's second busiest port, lies on the Indus delta creeks southeast of Karachi.

text: The Khewra Salt Mine is located in which district?
explanation: Khewra, in Jhelum district of Punjab, is one of the largest rock-salt mines in the world.

text: The Saindak copper and gold project is located in which district?
explanation: Saindak lies in Chagai district of Balochistan near the Iranian and Afghan borders.

text: The Sui gas field lies in which district of Balochistan?
explanation: Sui is located in Dera Bugti district in eastern Balochistan.

text: The Mari gas field is located in which province?
explanation: The Mari gas field lies near Daharki in the Ghotki area of upper Sindh.

text: The Thar coalfield is located in which province?
explanation: The Thar lignite deposits in Tharparkar district of Sindh are among the largest coal reserves in the world.

text: Muslim Bagh, known for chromite mining, is located in which province?
explanation: Muslim Bagh in Killa Saifullah district of Balochistan is Pakistan's main chromite producing area.

text: Emerald mines in Pakistan are chiefly located in which valley?
explanation: The emerald deposits near Mingora in the Swat valley are Pakistan's best known source of the gemstone.

text: Kalabagh, known for its iron ore deposits, lies in which district?
explanation: The Kalabagh iron ore field is in Mianwali district of Punjab on the right bank of the Indus.

text: The Deosai Plains are located in
explanation: Deosai, near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan, is one of the highest plateaus in the world and a national park.

text: The Salt Range lies between the Jhelum River and which other river?
explanation: The Salt Range stretches across northern Punjab between the Jhelum and the Indus, south of the Potohar Plateau.

text: The largest national park of Pakistan by area is
explanation: Hingol National Park on the Makran coast of Balochistan is the largest national park in Pakistan.

text: Astola Island, the largest island of Pakistan, lies off the coast of
explanation: Astola, also called Jezira Haft Talar, lies in the Arabian Sea off the Makran coast near Pasni.

text: The capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is
explanation: Muzaffarabad, on the confluence of the Neelum and Jhelum rivers, is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

text: Changa Manga, one of the largest planted forests of Pakistan, is located in which province?
explanation: Changa Manga is a man-made irrigated plantation in Kasur district of Punjab.

text: The monsoon rains in Pakistan generally occur between
explanation: The summer monsoon reaches Pakistan in early July and withdraws by September, bringing most of the annual rainfall.

text: The largest food crop of Pakistan in terms of area sown is
explanation: Wheat, a Rabi crop, occupies the largest cultivated area and is the staple food grain of Pakistan.

text: The province producing the largest share of Pakistan's cotton is
explanation: Punjab's southern districts account for the greater part of national cotton output, with Sindh second.

text: Faisalabad is popularly known as
explanation: Faisalabad earned the title because of its concentration of cotton textile mills.

text: Sialkot is chiefly known for the manufacture of
explanation: Sialkot is the centre of Pakistan's sports goods, leather and surgical instrument industries.

text: Pakistan Steel Mills was set up with the technical and financial assistance of
explanation: The Karachi steel mill was built at Pipri under a 1971 agreement with the Soviet Union.

text: The Heavy Mechanical Complex of Pakistan is located at
explanation: The Heavy Mechanical Complex at Taxila, built with Chinese assistance, manufactures industrial plant and machinery.

text: Pakistan's first nuclear power plant, KANUPP, began operating in
explanation: The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, built with Canadian assistance, was commissioned in 1972.

text: The State Bank of Pakistan was established on
explanation: The State Bank of Pakistan was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah on 1 July 1948.

text: The fiscal year of the Government of Pakistan runs from
explanation: Pakistan's financial year begins on 1 July and closes on 30 June.

text: The largest single category of Pakistan's exports is
explanation: Textiles and made-up garments have long accounted for roughly three-fifths of Pakistan's export earnings.

text: The largest group of Pakistan's imports by value is
explanation: Petroleum crude and refined products form Pakistan's biggest import bill and drive its trade deficit.

text: The Economic Survey of Pakistan is published each year by the
explanation: The Ministry of Finance issues the Economic Survey a day before the federal budget is presented.

text: The Pakistan Stock Exchange was created in 2016 by merging the stock exchanges of
explanation: The Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges were integrated into the Pakistan Stock Exchange in January 2016.

text: The nationalization of major industries, banks and insurance companies in Pakistan was carried out under
explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government began nationalizing basic industries in 1972 and banks in 1974.

text: The Green Revolution in Pakistan's agriculture took place mainly during the government of
explanation: High-yielding seed varieties, tubewells and fertilizer use spread rapidly in the 1960s under Ayub Khan.

text: Pakistan's First Five Year Plan covered the period
explanation: The First Five Year Plan ran from 1955 to 1960, though it was formally approved only in 1957.

text: The Motorway M-2 connects Islamabad with
explanation: The M-2, Pakistan's first motorway, links Islamabad with Lahore and was opened in 1997.

text: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor links Gwadar with which Chinese city?
explanation: CPEC connects Gwadar port to Kashgar in China's Xinjiang region by road, rail and pipeline routes.

text: The main CPEC agreements were signed in April 2015 during the visit to Pakistan of
explanation: Chinese President Xi Jinping's April 2015 visit produced the package of CPEC agreements worth about 46 billion dollars.

text: The operational control of Gwadar Port was transferred in 2013 to a company of
explanation: Operations passed from the Port of Singapore Authority to the China Overseas Ports Holding Company in 2013.

text: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in
explanation: The treaty was signed on 19 September 1960 after nine years of negotiation.

text: The Indus Waters Treaty was negotiated through the good offices of
explanation: The World Bank mediated the dispute and remains a signatory and guarantor of the treaty.

text: Under the Indus Waters Treaty the eastern rivers allotted to India are
explanation: India received unrestricted use of the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan received the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

text: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed on behalf of Pakistan by
explanation: President Ayub Khan signed for Pakistan and Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru for India.

text: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in which city?
explanation: The treaty was signed at Karachi, then the capital of Pakistan, in September 1960.

text: The body established under the Indus Waters Treaty to handle routine questions between the two countries is the
explanation: Each country appoints an Indus Commissioner, and together they form the Permanent Indus Commission.

text: The ceasefire ending the first Kashmir war between Pakistan and India came into effect on
explanation: A United Nations sponsored ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949 and produced the ceasefire line in Kashmir.

text: The 1965 war between Pakistan and India on the international border began on
explanation: Indian forces crossed the international border towards Lahore on 6 September 1965, now observed as Defence Day.

text: The Pakistani operation launched in Kashmir in August 1965 was code-named
explanation: Operation Gibraltar sent infiltrators into Indian-held Kashmir and led to the escalation of the 1965 war.

text: The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed in
explanation: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed the declaration on 10 January 1966.

text: The Tashkent talks of 1966 were mediated by
explanation: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent in Soviet Uzbekistan.

text: Dhaka fell to Indian forces on
explanation: The Pakistani eastern command surrendered at Dhaka on 16 December 1971, ending the war in East Pakistan.

text: The Simla Agreement was signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and
explanation: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement with Pakistan's President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

text: Pakistan formally recognized Bangladesh in
explanation: Pakistan recognized Bangladesh in February 1974, shortly before the second Islamic Summit at Lahore.

text: The second Islamic Summit Conference was held in 1974 at
explanation: Lahore hosted the second summit of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference in February 1974.

text: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests of 28 May 1998 in the hills of
explanation: Five devices were detonated in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai district on 28 May 1998.

text: The first Prime Minister of Pakistan was assassinated in 1951 at
explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi, later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

text: The first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in October 1958 was
explanation: When martial law was proclaimed on 7 October 1958, General Ayub Khan was appointed Chief Martial Law Administrator.

text: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law in Pakistan on
explanation: Zia-ul-Haq removed the Bhutto government in Operation Fair Play on 5 July 1977.

text: General Zia-ul-Haq died in an air crash in 1988 near
explanation: The presidential aircraft crashed shortly after take-off from Bahawalpur on 17 August 1988.

text: The first woman to become Prime Minister of Pakistan was
explanation: Benazir Bhutto took office in December 1988 as the first woman prime minister of Pakistan.

text: The first general elections in Pakistan held on the basis of adult franchise took place in
explanation: The December 1970 polls were Pakistan's first direct general elections on universal adult franchise.

text: Which city served as the interim capital of Pakistan while Islamabad was under construction?
explanation: Rawalpindi functioned as the interim capital from 1959 until Islamabad was ready to receive the government.

text: Pakistan became a member of the United Nations on
explanation: Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, six weeks after independence.

text: The highest civil award of Pakistan is
explanation: Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil decoration, usually conferred on foreign heads of state and government.

text: The first recipient of Nishan-e-Haider was
explanation: Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed was awarded the first Nishan-e-Haider for gallantry in Kashmir in 1948.

text: The only officer of the Pakistan Air Force awarded the Nishan-e-Haider is
explanation: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas received the award for preventing the hijacking of his aircraft to India in 1971.

text: Captain Karnal Sher Khan was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for gallantry in
explanation: Captain Karnal Sher Khan received the award posthumously for his defence of positions in the Kargil sector in 1999.

text: The national flower of Pakistan is
explanation: Jasmine, known locally as chambeli, is the national flower of Pakistan.

text: The national tree of Pakistan is
explanation: The Himalayan cedar or deodar is the national tree of Pakistan.

text: The national animal of Pakistan is the
explanation: The markhor, a wild goat of the northern mountains, is Pakistan's national animal.

text: The national bird of Pakistan is the
explanation: The chukar partridge is recognized as the national bird of Pakistan.

text: The national sport of Pakistan is
explanation: Field hockey is Pakistan's national game, in which the country has won several Olympic and World Cup titles.

text: The words of Pakistan's national anthem were written by
explanation: Abu-al-Asar Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the lyrics of the Qaumi Taranah.

text: The music of Pakistan's national anthem was composed by
explanation: Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla composed the tune, which was approved before the lyrics were selected.

text: The national anthem of Pakistan was officially adopted in
explanation: The Qaumi Taranah was formally adopted in August 1954 and first broadcast on Radio Pakistan.

text: The national flag of Pakistan was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
explanation: The Constituent Assembly approved the design of the national flag on 11 August 1947.

text: The white stripe in the national flag of Pakistan represents
explanation: The vertical white band stands for the non-Muslim minorities of Pakistan, while the green field represents the Muslim majority.

text: After the 1971 war, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took over as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in which month?
explanation: Bhutto assumed the offices of President and Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971, after Yahya Khan resigned in the wake of the loss of East Pakistan.

text: On behalf of Pakistan, the Instrument of Surrender at Dhaka on 16 December 1971 was signed by which officer?
explanation: Lt. Gen. A.A.K. Niazi, commander of Pakistani forces in the East, signed the Instrument of Surrender before Indian Lt. Gen. Jagjit Singh Aurora.

text: Following the 1971 war, approximately how many Pakistani military and civilian personnel were held as prisoners of war by India?
explanation: India held around 93,000 Pakistani prisoners of war and civilian internees, who were repatriated over the following two years under the Simla Agreement framework.

text: The Hamoodur Rahman Commission was set up by the Government of Pakistan to inquire into which event?
options: The circumstances of the 1971 war and the fall of Dhaka
explanation: Headed by Chief Justice Hamoodur Rahman, the commission investigated the causes of the military defeat in East Pakistan in 1971.

text: Under the Simla Agreement of 1972, the ceasefire line in Kashmir was renamed as the
explanation: The 1972 Simla Agreement between Pakistan and India renamed the earlier ceasefire line in Kashmir as the Line of Control.

text: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's land reforms of 1972 fixed the ceiling on individual landholding at how many acres of irrigated land?
explanation: The 1972 land reforms reduced the permissible ceiling to 150 acres of irrigated land and 300 acres of unirrigated land.

text: The Pakistan National Alliance, an opposition coalition formed after the disputed general election of 1977, was formed to oppose the government of which party?
explanation: The Pakistan National Alliance was a multi-party coalition formed to protest the Pakistan Peoples Party's victory in the March 1977 elections.

text: In which year was former Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto executed?
explanation: Bhutto was hanged on 4 April 1979 at Rawalpindi after being convicted of conspiracy to murder.

text: General Zia-ul-Haq formally assumed the office of President of Pakistan in
explanation: Zia-ul-Haq became President on 16 September 1978, succeeding Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry.

text: The Hudood Ordinances, introducing Islamic criminal punishments into Pakistani law, were promulgated in
explanation: The Hudood Ordinances were promulgated by General Zia-ul-Haq's government in February 1979.

text: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, providing for compulsory deduction of zakat, was introduced in
explanation: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance was promulgated in 1980 as part of General Zia-ul-Haq's Islamization measures.

text: The Movement for the Restoration of Democracy (MRD), an alliance of opposition parties against military rule, was launched in
explanation: The MRD was formed in 1981 to campaign for an end to General Zia-ul-Haq's martial law and the restoration of democratic government.

text: The long-running military standoff between Pakistan and India over the Siachen Glacier began in
explanation: Fighting over Siachen began in April 1984 after Indian forces occupied the glacier, making it one of the world's highest battlegrounds.

text: General Zia-ul-Haq held a national referendum seeking a mandate for his Islamization programme and continuation in office in
explanation: The referendum was held in December 1984, with the government claiming overwhelming public endorsement.

text: Pakistan's first general election held on a non-party basis under General Zia-ul-Haq took place in
explanation: The February 1985 elections were held without party affiliation on the ballot, after which Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister.

text: Prime Minister Muhammad Khan Junejo's government was dismissed by President Zia-ul-Haq in
explanation: Zia-ul-Haq dismissed the Junejo government on 29 May 1988, shortly before his own death in an air crash.

text: The 1988 Ojhri Camp disaster, in which an ammunition depot exploded causing heavy casualties, took place in which city?
explanation: The explosion at the Ojhri Camp ammunition store occurred in Rawalpindi in April 1988, killing more than a hundred people.

text: Benazir Bhutto's first government was dismissed by President Ghulam Ishaq Khan in
explanation: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan dismissed Benazir Bhutto's first government in August 1990 on charges of corruption and misgovernance.

text: Nawaz Sharif was sworn in as Prime Minister of Pakistan for the first time in
explanation: Nawaz Sharif first became Prime Minister in November 1990, after his alliance won the elections that followed Benazir Bhutto's dismissal.

text: In July 1993, President Ghulam Ishaq Khan and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif both resigned under an arrangement brokered by the Chief of Army Staff, General
explanation: General Abdul Waheed Kakar mediated the political deadlock, leading both the President and the Prime Minister to resign and a caretaker government to be installed.

text: Benazir Bhutto's second government was dismissed by President Farooq Leghari in
explanation: President Farooq Leghari dismissed Benazir Bhutto's second government in November 1996 amid allegations of corruption.

text: The military takeover led by General Pervez Musharraf that removed the government of Nawaz Sharif took place on
explanation: General Pervez Musharraf assumed power on 12 October 1999 after his removal as Army Chief was blocked and the government was overthrown.

text: The Kargil conflict between Pakistani and Indian forces in the mountains of Indian-administered Kashmir took place in
explanation: Fighting in the Kargil sector occurred between May and July 1999, ending after international pressure led to a Pakistani withdrawal.

text: General Pervez Musharraf held a referendum seeking public endorsement to continue as President for a further five years in
explanation: The referendum was held in April 2002 and was used to extend Musharraf's presidency.

text: The 2007 Lawyers' Movement in Pakistan primarily demanded the restoration of which suspended Chief Justice?
explanation: The lawyers' agitation of 2007-09 sought the reinstatement of Chief Justice Iftikhar Muhammad Chaudhry, who was eventually restored in March 2009.

text: The security operation against militants holed up in Islamabad's Lal Masjid (Red Mosque) took place in
explanation: The operation, launched in July 2007, ended a prolonged standoff between security forces and armed militants at the mosque complex.

text: Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated in December 2007 while campaigning in
explanation: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated after an election rally in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.

text: The general election of February 2008, which ended General Musharraf's period as an army-backed President, was won by which party?
explanation: The Pakistan Peoples Party won the largest number of seats in the 2008 election and led the coalition government that followed.

text: The devastating earthquake that struck northern Pakistan on 8 October 2005 was centred near
explanation: The epicentre lay near Muzaffarabad in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and the quake killed over 70,000 people across the region.

text: The catastrophic floods of 2010, among the worst in Pakistan's history, were caused by exceptionally heavy monsoon rains along which river system?
explanation: Heavy monsoon rains swelled the Indus and its tributaries, submerging large areas from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa down to Sindh.

text: Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden was killed by a US special forces raid in May 2011 in which Pakistani city?
explanation: The raid took place in Abbottabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on 2 May 2011.

text: The attack on the Army Public School in Peshawar, one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history, occurred in
explanation: Militants attacked the school on 16 December 2014, killing over a hundred students and staff.

text: Operation Zarb-e-Azb, a major military offensive against militant strongholds, was launched in June 2014 in
explanation: The operation targeted militant sanctuaries in North Waziristan following an attack on Karachi airport.

text: Pakistan's nuclear weapons tests of May 1998 were officially given which code name?
explanation: The six underground tests conducted on 28 May 1998 were officially designated Chagai-I.

text: Pakistan's first indigenously developed satellite, Badr-1, was launched in
explanation: Badr-1 was launched on 16 July 1990 aboard a Chinese Long March rocket, making Pakistan one of the first developing countries to build and operate its own satellite.

text: The Economic Cooperation Organization, formed in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, succeeded an earlier grouping known as
explanation: ECO succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development, which the three countries had formed in 1964.

text: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), of which Pakistan is a founding member, was established in
explanation: SAARC was founded in 1985 at a summit in Dhaka, bringing together seven South Asian states including Pakistan.

text: Following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, Pakistan began hosting very large numbers of Afghan refugees from
explanation: After the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan in December 1979, millions of Afghan refugees crossed into Pakistan over the following decade.

text: Pakistan formally joined the US-led international coalition against terrorism following the attacks of
explanation: Pakistan became a key ally in the campaign against terrorism after the September 11, 2001 attacks in the United States.

text: Which language is the mother tongue of the majority of the population in Punjab province?
explanation: Punjabi is the predominant first language spoken in Punjab, Pakistan's most populous province.

text: Which language is predominantly spoken in Sindh province?
explanation: Sindhi is the principal language of Sindh and one of the oldest written languages of the subcontinent.

text: Pashto is the predominant language of which province of Pakistan?
explanation: Pashto is spoken by the majority of the population in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and by Pashtun communities in northern Balochistan.

text: Balochi and Brahui are the two major languages spoken in
explanation: Balochi and Brahui, two linguistically unrelated languages, are both widely spoken across Balochistan.

text: Shina, Balti and Burushaski are among the languages spoken in
explanation: Gilgit-Baltistan is linguistically diverse, with Shina, Balti, Burushaski and Wakhi all spoken across its valleys.

text: Basant, a traditional kite-flying festival historically associated with Lahore, marks the arrival of which season?
explanation: Basant traditionally celebrated the coming of spring and was especially popular in Punjab.
